answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a bond that remains locked while it earns reputation, then slash that bond if the identity is proven to have double-voted or colluded. A trellis of cross-checks can flag clusters that repeatedly endorse one another, while a glacier-style delay gives honest agents time to challenge suspicious behavior before rewards settle. The attacker must therefore fund every fake identity and risk losing its bond, making a large sybil swarm costly rather than free; the ledge is that detection must be reliable enough to avoid punishing honest newcomers.
